item.title: France Blames Iran for Supermarket Hacks and Regional Sabotage: On Air, November 10, 2026
item.description:
France accused Iran of orchestrating a destructive cyberattack that struck commercial refrigeration units in 700 grocery stores on October 11 and 12. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called the operation an act of aggression and summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris. The Paris prosecutor's office opened a formal judicial investigation into the Shahid Kaveh offensive cyber unit.
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a press briefing in Paris on Tuesday that Washington does not need to conduct major combat operations against Iran. Rubio pointed to economic sanctions and a naval blockade as successful measures exerting extraordinary economic pressure. The remarks followed closed door talks in Washington involving President Donald Trump and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.
At least 12 people died and around 50 others were injured in multiple crashes involving between 50 and 86 vehicles on the Trakia motorway in southeastern Bulgaria on Tuesday. Health Minister Katya Ivkova stated that 10 or 11 people died at the scene near Yambol and Zimnitsa, while another victim died during transport or in hospital. Prime Minister Rumen Radev declared Wednesday a day of national mourning following the disaster.
The United States military relocated at least 10 aircraft from Royal Air Force Mildenhall in Suffolk, England, following a security threat linked to Iran. The operation marks the second withdrawal of American aircraft from a British base in three months following the removal of bombers from RAF Fairford in September. Security threat levels at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath were raised to FPCON Charlie.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth denounced an impeachment push as a political spectacle during a press conference at the Pentagon on Tuesday. The House of Representatives scheduled a vote on a resolution to impeach Hegseth after outgoing Representative Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment. Vice President JD Vance and President Donald Trump both defended Hegseth and condemned the effort.
President Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff following the departure of Susie Wiles. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the choice an absurd mistake and linked midterm losses to immigration policy management. Katie Miller ended business roles and sold shares in media and technology firms following the promotion.
Russia and Ukraine held four hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, marking their first trilateral negotiations in nine months. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy both described the initial session in positive terms while emphasizing that work remains. The talks focused on humanitarian measures, prisoner exchanges, and security guarantees.
California voters rejected Proposition 40, a ballot measure that sought to impose a one-time five percent tax on state residents with a net worth exceeding one billion dollars. Decision Desk HQ and the Associated Press projected the defeat after nearly 53 percent of voters opposed the measure. Google co-founder Sergey Brin contributed over one hundred million dollars to the opposition campaign.
China's cumulative trade surplus surpassed one trillion dollars in the first ten months of the year, driven by strong global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing goods. Customs data released on Tuesday showed that October exports jumped 35.2 percent year-on-year, while imports increased by 41.6 percent. The monthly trade surplus narrowed to 105.3 billion dollars.
An explosion at the Habas steel plant in Aliaga, Turkey, killed 18 workers and injured approximately a dozen others.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Paraguay Impeaches President as Digital Bank Collapses: On Air, November 9, 2026
item.description:
Seven people died and at least one hundred twenty-five others suffered injuries on Sunday when two passenger trains collided south of Cairo in the al Ayyat district of Giza province. A train traveling toward Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a stationary train heading toward Aswan province, causing several carriages to derail and overturn. The Chief Prosecutor office confirmed that the train conductor died in the crash, while emergency medical teams deployed more than fifty ambulances to the site.
President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles as she transitions to his political operation. The promotion prompted the immediate resignation of White House Deputy Chief of Staff Richard Walters, who served in the role since May and worked alongside Wiles for more than a decade. Katie Miller, the wife of Stephen Miller, announced she is pausing her podcast following her husband's promotion.
Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested a new passport and national identity card through her lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers in a letter addressed to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at Bangladesh embassy in Delhi. The communication marks her first formal contact with authorities since fleeing to self-imposed exile in India following a deadly student-led uprising in August 2024. The request aims to facilitate her planned return to Bangladesh in December, where she intends to surrender before a court.
President Donald Trump acknowledged that his administration mass deportation agenda was too tough and ultimately damaged the Republican Party during the midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats gaining control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Speaking during a CBS sixty minutes interview that aired Sunday night, Trump stated that while closing the border and removing criminal immigrants earned him high marks, taking people with good jobs who committed the sole violation of entering illegally proved too severe.
The Paraguayan Senate voted unanimously to remove President Santiago Pena from office following the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank. The crisis began after the Central Bank of Paraguay ordered Ueno Bank into a resolution process on Monday, November 3, after finding that its solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum, locking nearly three million customers out of their savings in a country of six and a half million people. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as president to serve the remainder of Pena term ending in August 2028.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the United States war against Iran during comments in Florida before departing for a Group of Seven foreign ministers meeting in Paris. Rubio stated that President Donald Trump launched the military campaign to safeguard the world from Iranian nuclear ambitions despite the conflict not being necessarily popular. Voters blamed the administration policies, including higher energy prices linked to the Strait of Hormuz, for economic hits during Tuesday elections that delivered a resounding rebuke to the administration.
Laura Gallacher arrived at Southwark Crown Court in London ahead of the sentencing hearing for her husband Russell Brand, who faces a lengthy prison term following his conviction for rape and sexual assault. Brand was found guilty by a jury of raping a twenty-one-year-old fan in 2009 at his Hampstead home and sexually assaulting three female television and radio workers between 2004 and 2009. Judge Justice Bennathan remanded Brand in custody immediately after the verdicts following a four-week trial.
